scope: CI diagnosis before further DIG runtime changes
problem: Node and Swift workflow jobs are failing with steps=null, so current evidence cannot distinguish hosted-runner provisioning failure from project code regressions.

independent_reviews.assessment: Best fault isolation. If this job also has no steps, project checkout/tests cannot be the cause. If it runs, investigation moves back to workflow/project bootstrap.

independent_reviews.candidate: revert recent reliability/security code until CI turns green
independent_reviews.assessment: Rejected. There is no failing assertion or compiler diagnostic tying recent runtime changes to the failure; reverting security gates without evidence increases regression and security risk.
Rejected for first diagnosis. It consumes more runners and duplicates maintenance. The minimal probe uses two short jobs, no checkout, no package install, and no third-party actions.

why_it_won.correctness: Separates runner allocation/execution from repository code and action dependencies.
why_it_won.robustness: Fails independently of npm, Node setup, checkout, Xcode project state, and DIG runtime code.
why_it_won.latency: Only shell metadata plus swift --version on macOS; expected runtime is seconds once a runner is allocated.
why_it_won.resource_use: Two short hosted jobs; no dependency installation or test suite execution.

failure_lessons: A red CI badge without workflow steps is not sufficient evidence of a code regression.
Do not weaken queue, qrexec, attestation, or iPhone controls without a concrete failing assertion/compiler diagnostic.
Runner health must be established before interpreting full-suite failures.
next_gate: Require ubuntu-runner and macos-runner preflight jobs to execute at least one step. If either still returns steps=null, treat GitHub-hosted runner/account provisioning as the blocker; if both execute, re-run Node/Swift QA and isolate the first failing project step.
